messages:
jamie_support: Heads-up — onboarding customer reported repeated SSE disconnects overnight. They see partial responses (truncated chunks), then a reconnect storm that explodes token billing. Token usage jumped 4x in 30m. Error pattern: some requests return `401` then client reconnects quickly and ends up re-requesting generation leading to duplication.

arjun_sre: Yikes. Any repro or request IDs?

jamie_support: I have a few request_ids from their logs: r-02a4c8, r-02a4d2, r-02a4ef. Timeline: token expired mid-stream (their auth refresh fails for ~2s), the client retries with new token immediately, server accepts but proxy (our ALB) drops some pending SSE frames. Client reopens and continues — but our backend already emitted tokens for the same prompt on a retry path.

laura_eng_runtime: Can you paste a minimal repro? Also: which client? Browser or server-side?

jamie_support: Browser single-page-app. Repro steps from customer (condensed):
1) Start SSE request with auth bearer token that is just about to expire.
2) Force token refresh to return new token during stream (they simulated by revoking token on auth server).
3) Client closes & reopens connection within 200-500ms.
4) Observe truncated output + duplicate tokens billed.

zack_devex: Do they use `Last-Event-ID` or application-level checkpointing? Without that the server can't resume; it will replay or start new generation.

jamie_support: They don't set Last-Event-ID. Their client expects resume semantics.

arjun_sre: Two related failure modes here: (A) auth handshake mid-stream causing client reconnect, (B) proxy/ALB behavior that can drop in-flight SSE frames when upstream connection is replaced. That can produce partial output on client + backend still finishing generation (billed).

mia_billing: From billing side: duplicate token charges show as near-identical timestamps and token counts for different request_ids. We need to correlate request_ids to compute dedup window. If client reconnects < X seconds we might be able to dedupe.

laura_eng_runtime: Technical notes: our runtime doesn't checkpoint generation mid-flight by default; the generator emits tokens and they're streamed as they arrive. If a connection is lost, generation may continue to completion depending on routing. We could add server-side short-circuiting when connection drops, but that risks wasted compute if client reconnects quickly.

arjun_sre: Proposed mitigation stack (short term -> long term):
- Short term: recommend client adopt `comment` ping (application-level heartbeat) every 15s and on reconnect include `Last-Event-ID` or generation id to request resume semantics. Also increase auth token leeway to avoid mid-stream expiry.
- Mid term: server detect auth-refresh reconnect storms (multiple connections with same session id within 1s) and throttle or tie to a single active generation.
- Long term: add resumable streaming protocol (generation checkpoints + resume token) + billing dedupe window.

zack_devex: Can we give them a concrete client patch/snippet?

jamie_support: Customer is OK to try a quick client change. Here's a minimal SSE client pattern we suggested:
```js
// send comment ping every 15s to keep proxies from closing
const es = new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true });
setInterval(() => {
  fetch('/sse/ping', {method: 'POST', headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`}, body: JSON.stringify({session_id})});
}, 15000);
// on reconnect include last event id
es.onopen = () => console.log('open');
es.addEventListener('message', e => lastEventId = e.lastEventId || lastEventId);
```
They'll send a lightweight POST to our API which we can treat as a keepalive if configured.

laura_eng_runtime: Note: comment pings as app-level keepalive are useful to keep ALB/Cloudflare idle timers happy, but they don't replace TCP keepalive. For mobile/browser clients, browser TCP keepalives are not configurable.

arjun_sre: Also worth noting: ALB has an idle timeout (e.g., 60s). If client or proxy closes and reopens quickly, ALB might still be finishing upstream connection; that can lead to mid-stream drop of frames.

mia_billing: For billing dedupe we need these fields logged on our side: session_id, generation_id, client_ip, upstream_connection_id. Can we add generation_id to X-Request-ID?

laura_eng_runtime: We can plumb generation_id into response headers and logs: `X-Gen-Id: gen-<hex>`. We'll add that as an experiment (flags: runtime.add-gen-id=true).

zack_devex: For immediate help for the customer: 1) increase auth token expiry leeway (server-side check) 2) add app-level comment ping 3) client: include Last-Event-ID on reconnect 4) enable `X-Gen-Id` logging flag so billing can correlate.

jamie_support: I rolled out a config change for that customer: token_leeway=10s and runtime.add-gen-id=true. They're testing now.

sse_watchdog_bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1345 — streaming reconnect spike detected 2067891200-2067894500. Linked request_ids: [r-02a4c8,r-02a4d2,r-02a4ef].

arjun_sre: Follow-ups for eng-runtime: add an experiment to cancel in-flight generations if upstream client disconnects and no reconnection within 800ms. Also add a short dedupe window (1s) where repeat generation requests with same session+prompt are considered retries and not double-billed.

laura_eng_runtime: Logged: I'll carve out a small spike to prototype `early-cancel` + `dedupe-window` flags. Need billing & SRE to own correctness criteria.

mia_billing: We'll provide a script to reconcile duplicates once gen-id is available. If you have sample logs (with request_ids) send DM and we'll diff.

jamie_support: Customer confirms reduced duplicates in preliminary run. They're still seeing rare partial outputs when reconnect <200ms. Will post more traces if they reproduce. Thanks team! :pray:

arjun_sre: Good. Action items:
- laura: prototype early-cancel + gen-id header (eta: 3d)
- mia: prepare billing dedupe script and window choices
- zack: publish a short devex note on recommended client patterns (comment ping, Last-Event-ID, backoff on reconnect)
- jamie: keep tracking customer reproductions and paste traces here.

zack_devex: I'll draft a KB entry and include a sample curl repro for them to run locally:
```bash
# simulate token refresh mid-stream
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?prompt=hello" \
  --max-time 120
# then revoke token on auth server after start and reconnect
```
jamie_support: Marking this thread for follow-up tomorrow. Closing for now unless customer reopens. :white_check_mark:
